paragraphs.text: Καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπέν μοι, καὶ τὴν φωνὴν αὐτοῦ ἤκουσα· Μὴ φοβοῦ, Ἑνὼχ, ἄνθρωπε ἀληθινὲ καὶ τῆς ἀληθείας γραμματεύς· πρόσελθε ὧδε καὶ ἄκουσον τὴν φωνήν μου.
paragraphs.translit: Kai apokritheis eipen moi, kai tēn phōnēn autou ēkousa; Mē phobou, Henōch, anthrōpe alēthine kai tēs alētheias grammateu; proselthe hōde kai akouson tēn phōnēn mou.

i18n.en: And he answered me and spoke to me, and I heard his voice: Fear not, Enoch, you man of truth, scribe of truth — draw near here, and hear my voice.

paragraphs.text: καὶ πορεύου εἰπὲ τοῖς Ἐγρηγόροις τοῦ οὐρανοῦ, οἵτινες ἀπέστειλάν σε ἐρωτῆσαι περὶ αὐτῶν· Ὑμεῖς ὀφείλετε ἐρωτᾶν περὶ τῶν ἀνθρώπων, καὶ μὴ οἱ ἄνθρωποι περὶ ὑμῶν.
paragraphs.translit: kai poreuou eipe tois Egrēgorois tou ouranou, hoitines apesteilan se erōtēsai peri autōn; Hymeis opheilete erōtan peri tōn anthrōpōn, kai mē hoi anthrōpoi peri hymōn.

i18n.en: And go, say to the Watchers of heaven who have sent you to petition on their behalf: It is you who ought to petition on behalf of mankind, and not mankind on behalf of you.

paragraphs.text: Διὰ τί ἀφήκατε τὸν οὐρανὸν τὸν ὑψηλὸν τὸν ἅγιον τοῦ αἰῶνος, καὶ μετὰ τῶν γυναικῶν ἐκοιμήθητε, καὶ μετὰ τῶν θυγατέρων τῶν ἀνθρώπων ἐμιάνθητε, καὶ ἐλάβετε ἑαυτοῖς γυναῖκας, καὶ ὥσπερ οἱ υἱοὶ τῆς γῆς ἐποιήσατε, καὶ ἐγεννήσατε υἱοὺς γίγαντας;
paragraphs.translit: Dia ti aphēkate ton ouranon ton hypsēlon ton hagion tou aiōnos, kai meta tōn gynaikōn ekoimēthēte, kai meta tōn thygaterōn tōn anthrōpōn emianthēte, kai elabete heautois gynaikas, kai hōsper hoi huioi tēs gēs epoiēsate, kai egennēsate huious gigantas?

i18n.en: Why did you abandon the high, the holy, the eternal heaven, and lie with women, and defile yourselves with the daughters of men, and take wives to yourselves, and do as the sons of the earth do, and beget giant sons?

paragraphs.text: Καὶ ὑμεῖς ἁγιάσματα πνευμάτων ζώντων ἀθανάτων εἰς πάσας τὰς γενεὰς τοῦ αἰῶνος ὑπήρξατε, καὶ ἐν τῷ αἵματι τῶν γυναικῶν ἐμιάνθητε, καὶ ἐν αἵματι σαρκὸς ἐγεννήσατε, καὶ ἐν αἵματι ἀνθρώπων ἐπεθυμήσατε, καὶ ἐποιήσατε ὥσπερ ποιοῦσιν σὰρξ καὶ αἷμα.
paragraphs.translit: Kai hymeis hagiasmata pneumatōn zōntōn athanatōn eis pasas tas geneas tou aiōnos hypērxate, kai en tō haimati tōn gynaikōn emianthēte, kai en haimati sarkos egennēsate, kai en haimati anthrōpōn epethymēsate, kai epoiēsate hōsper poiousin sarx kai haima.

i18n.en: And you — though you were sanctuaries of living, immortal spirits throughout all the generations of the age — yet you defiled yourselves with the blood of women, and begot offspring in the blood of flesh, and lusted after the blood of men, and did as those who are flesh and blood do.

paragraphs.text: Διὰ τοῦτο ἔδωκα αὐτοῖς γυναῖκας, ἵνα σπείρωσιν εἰς αὐτὰς καὶ τεκνωθήσονται τέκνα ἐξ αὐτῶν, ἵνα μηδὲν ἐκλίπῃ αὐτοῖς ἀπὸ τῆς γῆς.
paragraphs.translit: Dia touto edōka autois gynaikas, hina speirōsin eis autas kai teknōthēsontai tekna ex autōn, hina mēden eklipē autois apo tēs gēs.

i18n.en: Therefore I gave them wives, that they might sow seed in them, and that children might be born of them, so that nothing should fail them upon the earth.

paragraphs.text: Ὑμεῖς δὲ τὸ πρῶτον πνευματικοὶ ζῶντες αἰωνίως ἀθάνατοι εἰς πάσας τὰς γενεὰς τοῦ αἰῶνος ὑπήρχετε.
paragraphs.translit: Hymeis de to prōton pneumatikoi zōntes aiōniōs athanatoi eis pasas tas geneas tou aiōnos hypērchete.

i18n.en: But you from the beginning were spiritual, living an eternal life, immortal throughout all the generations of the age.

paragraphs.text: διὰ τοῦτο οὐκ ἐποίησα ἐν ὑμῖν θηλείας· οἱ πνευματικοὶ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ, ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ ἡ κατοίκησις αὐτῶν.
paragraphs.translit: dia touto ouk epoiēsa en hymin thēleias; hoi pneumatikoi tou ouranou, en tō ouranō hē katoikēsis autōn.

i18n.en: Therefore I did not make females among you; the spiritual ones of heaven — their dwelling is in heaven.

paragraphs.text: Καὶ νῦν οἱ γίγαντες οἱ γεννηθέντες ἀπὸ τῶν πνευμάτων καὶ σαρκὸς, πνεύματα ἰσχυρὰ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς καλέσουσιν αὐτούς, καὶ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ἔσται ἡ κατοίκησις αὐτῶν.
paragraphs.translit: Kai nyn hoi gigantes hoi gennēthentes apo tōn pneumatōn kai sarkos, pneumata ischyra epi tēs gēs kalesousin autous, kai epi tēs gēs estai hē katoikēsis autōn.

i18n.en: And now the giants, who have been born of spirits and flesh — they shall be called evil spirits upon the earth, and their dwelling shall be upon the earth.

paragraphs.commentary: **The foundational demonological etiology of Second-Temple Judaism and Patristic Christianity.** The disembodied spirits of the dead giants become the evil-spirits / demons of the post-flood world: 'the spirits of the giants ... shall be called evil spirits upon the earth; they shall be called evil spirits; for their dwelling shall be upon the earth and within the earth; evil spirits proceeded from their bodies, because they were born from above and the beginning of their creation was from the holy Watchers' (1 En 15:8-9). The etiology supplies the framework that Jub 10, Justin Martyr *2 Apol* 5, Athenagoras, and Tertullian *De Idololatria* 9 all develop systematically. See central entry `giants-become-evil-spirits-demonology-1-enoch-15-cross-corpus-jub-10-tertullian`.

paragraphs.text: πνεύματα πονηρὰ ἐκ τοῦ σώματος αὐτῶν ἐξελεύσονται, διότι ἀπὸ τῶν ἄνωθεν γεγένηνται, καὶ ἐκ τῶν ἁγίων Ἐγρηγόρων ἡ ἀρχὴ τῆς κτίσεως αὐτῶν καὶ ἀρχὴ θεμελίου, πνεύματα πονηρὰ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ἔσται, καὶ πνεύματα πονηρὰ καλέσουσιν αὐτά.
paragraphs.translit: pneumata ponēra ek tou sōmatos autōn exeleusontai, dioti apo tōn anōthen gegenēntai, kai ek tōn hagiōn Egrēgorōn hē archē tēs ktiseōs autōn kai archē themeliou, pneumata ponēra epi tēs gēs estai, kai pneumata ponēra kalesousin auta.

i18n.en: Evil spirits shall come forth out of their bodies, because they were born from those above; and from the holy Watchers is the beginning of their creation and their first foundation. Evil spirits they shall be upon the earth, and they shall be called evil spirits.

paragraphs.text: Τὰ πνεύματα τοῦ οὐρανοῦ ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ ἡ κατοίκησις αὐτῶν, καὶ τὰ πνεύματα τὰ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς γεννώμενα ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ἡ κατοίκησις αὐτῶν.
paragraphs.translit: Ta pneumata tou ouranou en tō ouranō hē katoikēsis autōn, kai ta pneumata ta epi tēs gēs gennōmena epi tēs gēs hē katoikēsis autōn.

i18n.en: The spirits of heaven — their dwelling is in heaven; but the spirits born on the earth — their dwelling is on the earth.

paragraphs.text: καὶ τὰ πνεύματα τῶν γιγάντων νεφέλας ἀδικοῦντα φθείροντα προσπίπτοντα μαχόμενα καὶ συντρίβοντα ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς, καὶ λύπην ποιοῦντα· καὶ οὐκ ἐσθίοντα οὐθέν, ἀλλὰ ἀσιτοῦντα, καὶ διψῶντα, καὶ προσκόπτοντα.
paragraphs.translit: kai ta pneumata tōn gigantōn nephelas adikounta phtheironta prospiptonta machomena kai syntribonta epi tēs gēs, kai lypēn poiounta; kai ouk esthionta outhen, alla asitounta, kai dipsōnta, kai proskoptonta.

i18n.en: And the spirits of the giants — wronging the clouds, corrupting, attacking, fighting, and crushing upon the earth, and causing grief — eat nothing, but they hunger and thirst, and they cause offense.

paragraphs.commentary: The catalog of demonic-activities: 'afflict, oppress, destroy, attack, do battle, work destruction on the earth, and cause trouble; they take no food, but nevertheless hunger and thirst, and cause offences' — the foundational Second-Temple-and-Patristic catalog of demonic-activities, supplying the framework for later Christian-monastic, Hekhalot-magical, and rabbinic demonologies.

paragraphs.text: Καὶ ἐξανίστανται ταῦτα τὰ πνεύματα ἐπὶ τοὺς υἱοὺς τῶν ἀνθρώπων καὶ ἐπὶ τὰς γυναῖκας, ὅτι ἐξεληλύθασιν ἀπ' αὐτῶν.
paragraphs.translit: Kai exanistantai tauta ta pneumata epi tous huious tōn anthrōpōn kai epi tas gynaikas, hoti exelēlythasin ap' autōn.

i18n.en: And these spirits shall rise up against the sons of men and against the women, because they have come forth from them.
